info.name: Purolator REST — Production
info.description:
**Verified live 2026-10-06** -- every request in this collection succeeded (REST content run in Certification). Requests that failed or were not sent are not included. On 2026-10-24 the REST requests were aligned with Purolator's published OpenAPI specs (exact enum spellings, developer notes in every description) without a new run. 13 request(s) marked *Spec-aligned 2026-10-24, not yet verified live* are included on that basis.

REST conversion of the Purolator SOAP surface, pointed at **https://shipapi.purolator.com**.

Production host. Live shipments are created — set validateOnly=true first when in doubt.

**Sources:** Purolator EWS *Developer Test Aid 2.0.0* (Corporate edition) plus the redactable call-and-answer samples.

**Before running:** set `REST_ClientId`, `REST_Secret` and `REST_XApiKey`, then run *00 · Auth → OKTA Token* to populate `REST_Token`.

**Create-shipment path:** `createShipmentPath` defaults to `/ship/v1/shipment`. Three variants appear in the existing STG collections (`/ship/v1/shipment`, `/shipping/v1/createshipment`, `/shipping/v1/shipment`) and they share one schema — switch by editing this one variable.


Identical to the Development edition apart from the host and `authScope`.

---
### Environment required
Select the matching environment before running — every credential, account number and date resolves from it, not from collection or global variables:

`SOAP_Key` · `SOAP_Password` · `REST_ClientId` · `REST_Secret` · `REST_XApiKey` · `REST_Token` · `AccountNumber` · `Different_AccountNumber` · `Current_Date`

**Dates** — the collection pre-request script sets `Current_Date` to today. Create- and validate-shipment requests override it with **today + 5 days**.

**Labels** — create-shipment and document requests carry a post-response script that decodes any base64 label in the response and renders it in the **Visualize** tab (ZPL via Labelary, PNG and PDF inline). Set `USE_LABELARY = false` in that script to keep label data off the third-party renderer.

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// PIN capture for the Document Matrix (folder 13).
// Each document type reads its PIN from its own environment variable, so
// the Document Matrix is identical in Certification, Development and
// Production -- only the captured values differ. This request is the
// source for the variables listed below.
// The Express Cheque receipt belongs to the cheque, not the parcel, so that
// seed prefers expressChequePIN and falls back to the shipment PIN.
// The PIN's field path differs between REST responses, so search for it
// rather than hard-code a path. Accepts "123", 123, and { "value": 123 }.
const hit = pinFrom(val, wanted);   // keep descending
try { docBody = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { docBody = null; }
// Most specific key first, so piecePINs can never win over the shipment PIN.
// The French twin leaves the shared PIN alone.
// pm.environment.set('PIN', capturedPin);      // keep the legacy single PIN fresh
// Leaving the previous value in place means a failed seed does not silently
// blank the matrix -- it reuses the last good PIN and says so.
console.log('[doc pin] no PIN in this response -- ' +
DOC_PIN_VARS.join(', ') + ' left at its previous value');
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

// blank the matrix -- it reuses the last good PIN and says so.

// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// PIN capture for the Document Matrix (folder 13).
// Each document type reads its PIN from its own environment variable, so
// the Document Matrix is identical in Certification, Development and
// Production -- only the captured values differ. This request is the
// source for the variables listed below.

// seed prefers expressChequePIN and falls back to the shipment PIN.
// The PIN's field path differs between REST responses, so search for it
// rather than hard-code a path. Accepts "123", 123, and { "value": 123 }.

// The French twin leaves the shared PIN alone.
// pm.environment.set('PIN', capturedPin);      // keep the legacy single PIN fresh
// Leaving the previous value in place means a failed seed does not silently
// blank the matrix -- it reuses the last good PIN and says so.
console.log('[doc pin] no PIN in this response -- ' +
DOC_PIN_VARS.join(', ') + ' left at its previous value');

// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name

const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}

// PIN capture for the SAMPLE document and tracking calls (fix_sample_contract.py R9).

if (Array.isArray(node)) { for (const x of node) { const h = pinFrom(x); if (h) return h; } return ''; }

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------
// PIN capture for the SAMPLE document and tracking calls (fix_sample_contract.py R9).
// Searches the response for the shipment PIN rather than hard-coding a path.
if (Array.isArray(node)) { for (const x of node) { const h = pinFrom(x); if (h) return h; } return ''; }
if (typeof v === 'string' || typeof v === 'number') return String(v);
if (v && typeof v === 'object' && v.value) return String(v.value);
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
if (pin) { PIN_VARS.forEach(v => pm.environment.set(v, pin)); console.log('[pin] ' + pin + ' -> ' + PIN_VARS.join(', ')); }
else { console.log('[pin] no shipmentPIN in the response; ' + PIN_VARS.join(', ') + ' left unchanged'); }

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// PIN capture for the Document Matrix (folder 13).
// Each document type reads its PIN from its own environment variable, so
// the Document Matrix is identical in Certification, Development and
// Production -- only the captured values differ. This request is the
// source for the variables listed below.
// The Express Cheque receipt belongs to the cheque, not the parcel, so that
// seed prefers expressChequePIN and falls back to the shipment PIN.
// The PIN's field path differs between REST responses, so search for it
// rather than hard-code a path. Accepts "123", 123, and { "value": 123 }.
const hit = pinFrom(val, wanted);   // keep descending
try { docBody = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { docBody = null; }
// Most specific key first, so piecePINs can never win over the shipment PIN.
// The French twin leaves the shared PIN alone.
// pm.environment.set('PIN', capturedPin);      // keep the legacy single PIN fresh
// Leaving the previous value in place means a failed seed does not silently
// blank the matrix -- it reuses the last good PIN and says so.
console.log('[doc pin] no PIN in this response -- ' +
DOC_PIN_VARS.join(', ') + ' left at its previous value');
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}

// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name

// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather

// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.

body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{/unless}}

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).

// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.

exec: // Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

exec: // Collection pre-request — runs before every request in the collection.
// Refreshes Current_Date to TODAY and mints a unique RequestReference.
// Create-shipment requests override Current_Date with today + 5 days in
// their own pre-request script, which runs after this one.
// Two-digit padding for the RequestReference stamp below. This line was
// deleted by the timezone patch in 3be7aa3, and every pre-request script
// in the collection threw `pad is not defined` from then until it was
// put back. Newman still SENDS the request when its pre-request script
// throws, so the run looked fine -- 11 requests executed, assertions
// passing -- while 11 of 11 pre-request scripts failed and
// RequestReference silently kept whatever stale value the environment
// already held. Check the prerequest-scripts row of Newman's summary
// table, not just the assertions row.
// Purolator validates the shipment date in ITS timezone. Using the
// runner's local date sends yesterday whenever the machine is west of
// Eastern late in the day, and the API rejects it (9001-11).
// Dates the merged support / STG requests use (2026-10-06), in the carrier's timezone.
// Next business day for pickups: skip Saturday (6) and Sunday (0).
pm.environment.set('manifestDate', today);          // summary manifest window: today-10 .. today
pm.environment.set('manifestDateOld', day(-11));    // just outside the window (expect 400)
pm.environment.set('shipmentDateFar', day(15));     // beyond the +10 day ship window (expect 400)
// REQ + YYYYMMDDHHMMSS, matching the convention used in the SOAP collections.
